Definition: from another form of the base of G3582; timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance:--staff, stocks, tree, wood.
BiblicalUsage: Judas came with a great multitude with swords and staves to take Jesus. The same word is used when Peter preaches that the God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the tree carries the whole gospel in one word: the staves that seized Him in the garden were wood, and the tree that held Him outside the city was wood, and God turned the timber of the arrest into the timber of the atonement. I believe the cross was not an accident of wood but the place where the tree became the altar.
